dualgoal.noteBase: Base phase – the ideal time to lose weight: a moderate deficit with plenty of easy volume.
dualgoal.noteBuild: Build phase – hard sessions need energy: a smaller deficit and plenty of protein to keep their quality up.
dualgoal.notePeak: Peak phase – performance comes first: keep the deficit small, or the quality of your sessions suffers.
dualgoal.noteTaper: Taper – refuel now instead of losing weight: eat well so you’re fit for race day.
dualgoal.stimulusEnough: Your training gives you enough stimulus for real progress.
dualgoal.stimulusLow: Not much challenging stimulus lately – rest days alone won’t bring you closer to your goal. Plan key sessions again (stimulus + recovery = progress).

fullBody.title: Full body
fullBody.desc: Full body, 3 rounds (bodyweight or with dumbbells/kettlebell): Squats 12× · Push-ups 8–12× (on your knees if needed) · Lunges 10×/leg · Shoulder press 12× · Plank 30–45 s. Clean technique before weight, 60–90 s rest between rounds.

legs.title: Legs & glutes
legs.desc: Leg strength for a stable running form, 3 rounds: Squats 15× · Romanian deadlift (dumbbell/kettlebell or single-leg) 10× · Step-ups onto a bench/step 10×/leg · Calf raises 20× (half of them with bent knees) · Glute bridge 15×. With weights a few reps fewer, 60–90 s rest.

core.title: Trunk & core
core.desc: Core stability for an upright running posture, 3 rounds: Plank 40 s · Side plank 30 s/side · Dead bug 10×/side · Bird dog 10×/side (on all fours, extend opposite arm and leg without arching your back) · Russian twists 20×. Slow and controlled, keep your body tension on purpose.

legsPush.title: Strength – Legs & pushing
legsPush.desc: 3–4 rounds: Squats or leg press 8–10× · Weighted lunges 10×/leg · Sled push or wall sit 45 s · Push-ups 10× · Plank 40 s. Heavy but clean – 90 s rest between rounds.

pullGrip.title: Strength – Pulling & grip
pullGrip.desc: 3–4 rounds: Romanian deadlift 8× · Bent-over row 10× · Farmer’s carry 2×30 m heavy · Lat pulldown or negative pull-ups 8× · Dead bug 10×/side. Grip strength pays off in the Farmer’s carry and the sled pull.

fullBody.title: Strength – Full body & wall balls
fullBody.desc: 3 rounds: Front squat or thrusters 10× · Wall balls 15× · Kettlebell swings 15× · Sandbag or dumbbell lunges 20 m · Burpees 8×. Brisk, but with clean technique.

readiness.past: This race is in the past – a plan can’t be created for it any more. Check the date.
readiness.today: It’s race day – too late for a training plan. Good luck!

short.one: For {race} at the “{level}” level we recommend at least {minWeeks} weeks of preparation – you have {count} week until the race. You could choose a later race, a shorter distance or the goal “finish healthy” without a target time. Either way, the plan only builds volume gently.
short.other: For {race} at the “{level}” level we recommend at least {minWeeks} weeks of preparation – you have {count} weeks until the race. You could choose a later race, a shorter distance or the goal “finish healthy” without a target time. Either way, the plan only builds volume gently.

hyroxRun.title: Hyrox running {n}×1 km
hyroxRun.desc: {warm} warm-up, then {n}×1 km brisk (Z4, around threshold pace) with {pause} rest after each – just like between the stations in the race: catch your breath after the kilometre, then find your pace again. {cool} cool-down.

baseRun.title: Easy run with strides
baseRun.desc: Easy run in Z2 (conversational pace). In the last 1–2 km, add 5–6 strides of ~80–100 m: jog in easily, accelerate over ~20 m to about 90 % (fast, but not a sprint), then let it roll out. Walk or jog easily for 60–90 s in between. Heart rate doesn’t matter here – it’s about speed and clean technique.

threshold.title: Threshold run {n}×{min} min
threshold.marathonDesc: Marathon-specific: {warm} easy warm-up. Then {n}×12 min at threshold (Z4, “comfortably hard”) with 3 min easy jogging after each – long, steady efforts instead of short peaks. {cool} cool-down. In a marathon, endurance at the upper end of your pace range is what counts.
threshold.desc6: {warm} easy warm-up (Z2). Then {n}×6 min at threshold (Z4, “comfortably hard” – you could still speak short sentences) at your target pace, with 2 min very easy jogging in between. Finish with {cool} cool-down. Stay even – don’t overdo the first interval.
threshold.desc8: {warm} easy, {n}×8 min at threshold (Z4) with 2 min jog recovery, {cool} cool-down. Keeps your speed endurance without draining your legs the way VO₂max intervals do.

fartlek.title: Fartlek {n}×(1 min fast / 1 min easy)
fartlek.desc: {warm} easy warm-up. Then {n}×1 min brisk (Z4, “comfortably hard”), with 1 min of very easy running in between (don’t stop) – a flowing fartlek. Hold the pace without sprinting. {cool} cool-down.

marathonPace.title: Marathon race pace {n}×4 km
marathonPace.desc: Race-pace specific: {warm} easy, then {n}×4 km at your target marathon pace (controlled but brisk) with 3 min easy jogging after each. {cool} cool-down. Practise eating & drinking as on race day.

hmPace.title: Half marathon pace {n}×3 km
hmPace.desc: Race-pace specific: {warm} easy warm-up, then {n}×3 km at your target half-marathon pace with 2 min easy jogging after each. {cool} cool-down. The pace should feel controlled – the way you want to hold it for 21 km on race day.

vo2.desc800: {warm} warm-up. Then {n}×800 m hard (Z5 – only single words possible) at your target pace, with ~2:30 min very easy jogging in between. {cool} cool-down. Keep all intervals at the same speed – better even than a first one that’s too fast.
vo2.title: VO2max {n}×{m} m
vo2.desc400: {warm} warm-up. Then {n}×400 m fast (Z5) around your 5 km race pace, with ~90 s very easy jogging in between. {cool} cool-down. Short, sharp, clean – the speed for your 5 km race.
vo2.desc1000: {warm} warm-up. {n}×1000 m hard (Z5) at 5–10 km pace, with ~2:30 min easy jogging in between. {cool} cool-down. Stay even all the way.

pyramid.title: VO2max pyramid {seq} min
pyramid.desc: {warm} warm-up. Then a pyramid: {seq} min hard (Z5) with 90 s very easy jogging after each. The {peak}-minute step in the middle is the high point – hold it evenly, don’t overdo it. {cool} cool-down.

pace10k.title: 10 km race pace {n}×1000 m
pace10k.desc: {warm} warm-up. Then {n}×1000 m at your target 10 km race pace with ~2:30 min jog recovery after each. {cool} cool-down. This is how race pace feels – controlled, not flat out.

taper.raceDesc: {warm} warm-up, {n}×2 km at race pace with 3 min jog recovery, {cool} cool-down. Remind your legs of the pace – the volume is deliberately small, your freshness now comes from recovery.
taper.tempoDesc: {warm} warm-up, {n}×{min} min at threshold (Z4) with a long 3 min break, {cool} cool-down. Keep the stimulus, cut the volume – your sharpness now comes from recovery.

runWalk.title: Run-walk {n}×{min} min
runWalk.desc: Walk briskly for 5 min, then {n}× alternate {min} min of easy running with 1 min of walking, and finish with 5 min of walking. Run at a pace where you can still chat – the walk breaks are part of the plan, not giving up.

walk.title: Brisk walk
walk.desc: 30 min brisk walking – active recovery that keeps your circulation going without loading your legs. Counts fully as exercise.

long.easyDesc: Calm and steady in Z2 – base endurance for the eight running kilometres between the stations. Pace doesn’t matter.
long.title: Long run {km}
long.bikeAlt: Bike alternative (also easy on your back): ~{from}–{to} km or 1.5–2.5 h easy in Z2 instead of the run.
long.bikeAltRaceBlock: Bike alternative (also easy on your back): ~{from}–{to} km or 1.5–2.5 h easy in Z2 – but then no extra bike ride today.
long.leadTaper: Taper – shorter than recently, build up freshness.
long.raceBlockDesc: {km} in total: start easy in Z2, run {block} at race pace{pace} in one go in the middle, then ease back into an easy finish. Practise eating & drinking as on race day.
long.finish: Run the last 2 km briskly at marathon pace – a small stimulus that teaches tired legs to hold the pace.
long.desc: Calm long run, steady in Z2 throughout – fat metabolism & base endurance. Take a few sips every 20 min.

swim.techDesc: {m} m warm-up, 6×50 m technique drills (e.g. catch-up, fist swimming), then {reps}×100 m brisk with 20 s rest, {m} m easy cool-down. Calm, long strokes and clean breathing – technique over rush.
swim.raceDesc: Swim the race distance ({m} m) once in one go at your planned race pace – ideally in open water (in a wetsuit if it’s allowed in the race). Warm up easily before, 200 m easy afterwards.
swim.enduranceDesc: Steady swimming: 3×{m} m with 30 s rest at a calm base pace. Practise sighting along the way (look ahead every 6–8 strokes).

bike.baseDesc: Steady in Z2, cadence ~85–95 – pedal in smooth circles, don’t stomp.
bike.buildDesc: After 15 min warm-up, 4×5 min at threshold (Z4) with 3 min easy spinning in between. Then cool down.
bike.peakDesc: After 15 min warm-up, 3×10 min at your planned race pace (Z3–Z4) with 3 min easy spinning in between. Then cool down.
bike.taperDesc: Easy in Z2 with 4×30 s brisk efforts along the way. Stay fresh.
bike.title: Bike training
bike.longDesc: Long, calm ride in Z2 (~{dur} min), eat & drink well.
bike.brick: Straight afterwards, run easy for 10–15 min (brick training) – so your legs get used to switching from bike to run.

hyrox.baseDesc: {rounds} rounds, four stations each at half race volume: SkiErg 500 m · Wall Balls 30× · Sandbag Lunges 40 m · Rowing 500 m. No running in between – technique before speed, 90 s rest per round. No sled? Weighted squats or a wall sit instead.
hyrox.buildDesc: {rounds} rounds: run 1 km briskly, then straight into a station – alternating SkiErg 1000 m, Sled Push 50 m (or squats 20×), Burpee Broad Jumps 40 m, Rowing 1000 m, Farmer’s carry 200 m, Wall Balls 50×. This teaches your legs to find your running pace again after a station.
hyrox.simDesc: {rounds}× (1 km at your planned race pace + one station in race order: SkiErg, Sled Push, Sled Pull, Burpee Broad Jumps, Rowing, Farmer’s carry, Sandbag Lunges, Wall Balls). Like on race day: start controlled, move quickly through the Roxzone, test your fuelling. Then two easy days.
hyrox.peakDesc: {rounds} rounds: one station at full race volume at your planned pace, then run 500 m briskly. 2 min rest between rounds. Start with your weakest stations.
hyrox.taperDesc: 4× (500 m brisk + half a station), 2 min rest. Stay fresh and let the routines settle.

near.shakeoutDesc: Very easy with a few strides. Wake your legs up before the race.
near.bikeCheckDesc: Spin easily, check gears and brakes, three short surges.
near.activationDesc: {warm} easy, 3×{min} min at race pace with 2 min jog recovery, 4 strides. Sharp but short.
near.easyShortDesc: Easy – stay fresh for the race.
near.lastLongerDesc: Calm in Z2 – your last slightly longer run before the race, no pace work.
near.swimDesc: Easy warm-up, 4×50 m at race pace, easy cool-down. Keep your feel for the water.
near.rideDesc: Easy in Z2 with 3×1 min at race pace in between.
near.brickDesc: 35 min easy on the bike, then straight into 10 min of easy running – keeps the transition familiar without tiring you.
near.hyroxDesc: One short technique round per station at half volume, no running at the limit. Go through the transitions and the order once more.

steadyRun.title: Steady easy run
steadyRun.desc: Steady in the base zone (Z2), conversational pace – you should be able to chat as you go. Rather a bit too slow than too fast; volume counts here, not pace.
steadyRun.backAlt: With back pain, do a steady bike ride (Z2) instead.

football.title: Football
football.desc: Team training – counts as cross-training (accelerations, speed, joy of the game). Warm up well, then jog easily for 5–10 min afterwards. If it was intense, take your next run a bit easier.

mobility.title: Mobility & stretching
mobility.desc: Calm mobility, 10–15 min, especially kind to your back: Cat-cow 10× · Hip flexor stretch 45 s/side · Gentle hamstring stretch 45 s/side · Calf stretch against the wall 45 s/side · Chest opener & supine twist 8×/side · Child’s pose 60 s. Nothing jerky – breathe gently into each position.

recovery.title: Recovery run
recovery.desc: Very easy in Z1–Z2, noticeably slower than your steady runs – if it feels “almost too easy”, it’s just right. Your legs should recover; pace doesn’t matter. Alternatively, an easy bike ride that’s gentle on your back.

extra.title: Easy run
extra.desc: Short and easy in Z2 – build volume without getting tired. No pace, no ambition.

tactic.5k: Start controlled (don’t overdo it!), pick it up from halfway and give everything in the last third.
tactic.10k: Even at race pace, pick it up bit by bit from km 7.
tactic.hm: Start evenly, give everything from km {km}.
tactic.marathon: Start deliberately conservatively and stay even – the race is decided from km {km}. Fuel as in training.

race.triDesc: Race day! {format}: {swim} m swim · {bike} km bike · {run} km run.{target} Swim: settle calmly into your rhythm, don’t burn out in the pack. Bike: steady, don’t overpace – you’ll still need your legs; drink regularly. Transitions quick but without rushing. Run: take the first 1–2 km deliberately easy, then build.
race.hyroxSplits: Guide values for {time}: about {run} min per running kilometre and about {station} min per station including the Roxzone.
race.hyroxDesc: Race day! 8 × 1 km running, with a station after each kilometre: SkiErg 1000 m · Sled Push 50 m · Sled Pull 50 m · Burpee Broad Jumps 80 m · Rowing 1000 m · Farmer’s carry 200 m · Sandbag Lunges 100 m · Wall Balls 100 reps (weights depending on your division).{target}{splits} Run the first kilometres deliberately controlled – the stations cost more than you think. Move quickly through the Roxzone but breathe calmly; do the wall balls in fixed sets with short breaks.

strides.title: Easy with strides
strides.raceWeekDesc: The activation run would sit right next to a hard fixed appointment – that appointment already wakes your legs up. So just easy in Z2 with 4 strides of ~20 s at the end. Stay fresh for the race.
strides.desc: This week your quality session would sit right next to a hard fixed appointment – the appointment provides the intensity. So an easy run in Z2 with 4–6 strides of ~20 s at the end (brisk, no sprinting; jog easily in between). That keeps your speed without two hard days in a row.

consolidate.name: Consolidate
consolidate.focus: Harder variations, lock in the habit

fitness.label: General fitness
fitness.desc: Endurance, strength and mobility following the WHO activity guidelines: endurance rises from about 120 to 150–180 minutes a week (brisk walking counts), plus strength on two days.

strength.label: Strength & muscle
strength.desc: Focus on strength training (alternating full-body sessions, two to three strength days) with some endurance and mobility for recovery. Strength progresses through rounds, reps and harder variations.

weightloss.label: Weight loss
weightloss.desc: Lots of movement (endurance and brisk walking, from about 150 to 225–240 minutes a week) plus strength on two days for your metabolism. Works best together with the calorie balance in Nutrition.

mobility.label: Mobility & health
mobility.desc: A gentle start: mobility, gentle strength on two days and activity that grows from about 90 to 150 minutes a week – ideal for beginners or for getting back into it.

fullBody.title: Strength – Full body
fullBody.moves: Squats 12× · Push-ups 8–12× (on your knees if needed) · Lunges 10×/leg · Shoulder press 12× · Plank 30–45 s
fullBody.harder: weighted squats, push-ups with feet raised, plank 60 s

lowerBody.title: Strength – Lower body
lowerBody.moves: Squats 15× · Romanian deadlift (dumbbell/kettlebell or single-leg) 10× · Step-ups onto a bench/step 10×/leg · Calf raises 20× · Glute bridge 15×
lowerBody.harder: Bulgarian split squats instead of step-ups, glute bridge on one leg, more weight

upperBody.title: Strength – Upper body & core
upperBody.moves: Push-ups 8–12× · Rows (dumbbell/band) 12× · Shoulder press 12× · Plank 40 s · Side plank 30 s/side · Dead bug 10×/side
upperBody.harder: close-grip push-ups, a stronger band or heavier dumbbell, side plank with leg raises

gentle.title: Gentle strength
gentle.moves: Sit-to-stand from a chair 10× · Wall push-ups 10× · Glute bridge 12× · Calf raises holding a chair 15× · On all fours, opposite arm and leg 8×/side
gentle.harder: lower more slowly, add short holds, only then more reps

strength.howEasy: Easier week: 2 rounds of your usual exercises, deliberately a little lighter.
strength.howIntro: Getting started: 2 rounds, technique before speed – better a few reps fewer, but clean.
strength.howBuild: 3 rounds. Every one to two weeks, add 1–2 reps or a little more weight, as long as your technique stays clean.
strength.desc: {how} Exercises per round: {moves}. 60–90 s rest between rounds.

block.total: About {minutes} min of endurance this week, walking included – the WHO recommends 150–300 min.
block.cardioDesc: Steady cardio at a conversational pace (Z2) – running, cycling, elliptical or swimming, whatever you like. You should be able to chat as you go. {total}
block.walkDesc: A brisk walk, ideally in the fresh air – fast enough that you breathe a little harder but can still talk. Easy to start and gentle on your joints, it counts fully as endurance. {total}
block.mobilityDesc: Calm mobility session: Cat-cow 10× · Hip flexor stretch 45 s/side · Gentle hamstring stretch 45 s/side · Chest opener & supine twist 8×/side · Child’s pose 60 s. Breathe gently into each position, nothing jerky.
